Contemporary demo reporting, trailer, preservation gameplay and a later x86-development recording survive. The 2008 BREW demo report uses generic BioShock key art and provides no show-floor still. Three original character and prop renders survive in Nitin Dhamse’s portfolio. Hidden Palace documents a level-map collection and editor, but the resource page reports an unavailable download and provides no map preview.

access_limits.note: MobyGames’ BREW gallery has no shots. Pocket Gamer supplied a contemporary Java preview still. No verifiable production drawings surfaced through Games on Deck’s Anna Kang interview, RPGFan, or the listed screenshot databases.

Pocket Gamer and My Abandonware identify their gallery images as Java. WIRED’s inline original image returned 404. DoCoMo’s promotional material depicts the distinct Japanese 3D port. Live Namco USA archive pages were not recovered in this pass.

GameFAQs mobile media page republishes PS2 box scans and GBA images. GameSpot’s mobile review and preview survive, but the migrated articles expose no period mobile gameplay image, and MobyGames’ J2ME gallery was empty.
GameSpot documents Sony Pictures Mobile’s V CAST NY Rooftops and NY Subway games. The catalog’s plain Spider-Man filename does not select one.

Legacy Superscape screenshot reposts on AVP Galaxy point to a redirect loop and a missing title image. The 2007 preview footage still works. My Abandonware and MobyGames galleries had no images for the 2006 BREW title.

Aurel Manea’s CV names him as lead 3D artist on the V CAST edition and separately identifies his DS credit. The dated carrier advertisement anchors the V CAST visuals. No project artwork was located in the public CV.
The Qualcomm conference deck is platform development evidence. Its Ducati and CarBen images do not establish any of the archived sample packages’ identities.
